intro: A collection of apocalyptic writings attributed to Enoch, the great-grandfather of Noah, composed in stages over several centuries and preserved complete only in Ge'ez.

facts.label: Composed
facts.value: c. 300 BCE – 1st century CE, in stages

facts.label: Original language
facts.value: Aramaic for most sections; preserved complete in Ge'ez

facts.label: Canonical status
facts.value: Scripture in the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

background.text: Genesis says Enoch "walked with God; and he was not, for God took him." Later Jewish writers credited him with visions of heaven, the angels, and the end of history. Aramaic fragments of most sections were found among the Dead Sea Scrolls at Qumran.
The Epistle of Jude quotes 1 Enoch 1:9 almost word for word.
Its picture of fallen angels, final judgment, and a heavenly "Son of Man" is widely seen as shaping early Christian thought.
